title: Part 2 Practice: Geological Processes and Landforms

questions.text: The OLDEST rocks in Ethiopia belong to which era?
questions.explanation: PRECAMBRIAN rocks are the OLDEST in Ethiopia (4.5 billion - 600 million years ago). These are the crystalline basement rocks (granite, gneiss, schist) found in northern, western, and southern Ethiopia.

questions.text: Precambrian rocks in Ethiopia are primarily:
options: B) Granite, gneiss, and schist (crystalline basement rocks)
questions.correct_answer: B) Granite, gneiss, and schist (crystalline basement rocks)
questions.explanation: Precambrian rocks underwent intense HEAT and PRESSURE (metamorphism), creating CRYSTALLINE rocks like granite, gneiss, and schist. Sandstone and limestone are SEDIMENTARY rocks from later eras. Volcanic basalt is from the Cenozoic era.

questions.text: During the PALEozoIC era, Ethiopia experienced:
options: B) Erosion of Precambrian mountains and deposition of sedimentary rocks
C) Formation of the Rift Valley
questions.correct_answer: B) Erosion of Precambrian mountains and deposition of sedimentary rocks
questions.explanation: The PALEozoIC era was a period of DENUDATION (wearing away) — mountains were ERODED to flat surfaces and sediments were deposited in shallow seas. Volcanic eruptions and Rift Valley formation happened in the CENOZOIC era.

questions.text: Examine the rock layer diagram. Which is the OLDEST rock?
questions.diagram: <svg width='350' height='180' viewBox='0 0 350 180'><rect width='350' height='180' fill='#111827' rx='8'/><text x='175' y='18' text-anchor='middle' fill='#f59e0b' font-size='11' font-weight='bold'>Rock Layers (Superposition)</text><rect x='60' y='30' width='230' height='25' rx='3' fill='#f43f5e'/><text x='175' y='48' text-anchor='middle' fill='#f8fafc' font-size='9'>Layer D (Top - Youngest)</text><rect x='60' y='60' width='230' height='25' rx='3' fill='#facc15'/><text x='175' y='78' text-anchor='middle' fill='#0B0F19' font-size='9'>Layer C</text><rect x='60' y='90' width='230' height='25' rx='3' fill='#14b8a6'/><text x='175' y='108' text-anchor='middle' fill='#f8fafc' font-size='9'>Layer B</text><rect x='60' y='120' width='230' height='25' rx='3' fill='#6d28d9'/><text x='175' y='138' text-anchor='middle' fill='#f8fafc' font-size='9'>Layer A (Bottom - Oldest)</text><text x='175' y='165' text-anchor='middle' fill='#94a3b8' font-size='9'>Which layer is Precambrian?</text></svg>
questions.explanation: According to SUPERPOSITION, the OLDEST rocks are at the BOTTOM. Layer A (bottom, purple) would be Precambrian — the oldest rocks. Layer D (top, red) is the youngest (Cenozoic).

questions.text: The MESOZOIC era is known for depositing which rocks in Ethiopia?
questions.explanation: During the MESOZOIC era, shallow seas covered much of Ethiopia, depositing SEDIMENTARY rocks: Adigrat Sandstone (from deserts) and Antalo Limestone (from marine environments). Granite/gneiss is Precambrian, volcanic basalt is Cenozoic.

questions.text: The Ethiopian PLATEAUX were formed by:
options: B) Uplifting of landmass and outpouring of lava (Cenozoic)
questions.correct_answer: B) Uplifting of landmass and outpouring of lava (Cenozoic)
questions.explanation: During the CENOZOIC era, tectonic forces UPLIFTED the Arabo-Ethiopian landmass, and huge quantities of LAVA (Trap Series basalt) poured out, creating the Ethiopian Plateaus. This was the most important event in shaping Ethiopia's current landscape.

questions.text: Examine the diagram. What does the CENTRAL depression represent?
questions.diagram: <svg width='350' height='160' viewBox='0 0 350 160'><rect width='350' height='160' fill='#111827' rx='8'/><rect x='20' y='40' width='100' height='70' rx='6' fill='#1a2332' stroke='#14b8a6' stroke-width='2'/><text x='70' y='70' text-anchor='middle' fill='#14b8a6' font-size='9' font-weight='bold'>Western Plateau</text><rect x='230' y='40' width='100' height='70' rx='6' fill='#1a2332' stroke='#f43f5e' stroke-width='2'/><text x='280' y='70' text-anchor='middle' fill='#f43f5e' font-size='9' font-weight='bold'>Eastern Plateau</text><path d='M 120 80 L 230 40 L 230 110 L 120 110 Z' fill='#facc15' opacity='0.6'/><text x='175' y='130' text-anchor='middle' fill='#facc15' font-size='9' font-weight='bold'>???</text></svg>
questions.explanation: The CENTRAL depression between the Western and Eastern Plateaus is the GREAT RIFT VALLEY. It formed when tectonic forces pulled the Earth's crust apart, creating a long, narrow depression through eastern Africa.

questions.text: The Rift Valley in Ethiopia runs in which direction?
questions.explanation: Ethiopia's Rift Valley runs from the NORTHEAST (Afar region) to the SOUTHWEST (Lake Turkana area). This NE-SW orientation is part of the larger East African Rift System.

questions.text: The QUATERNARY period is characterized by:
options: B) Continued volcanism, lake formation, and alluvial deposition
D) Complete cessation of geological activity
questions.correct_answer: B) Continued volcanism, lake formation, and alluvial deposition
questions.explanation: The QUATERNARY period (last 2.6 million years) saw CONTINUED volcanic activity in the Rift Valley (Erta Ale, Fantale), formation of Rift Valley lakes (Abaya, Chamo, Ziway), and deposition of alluvial sediments.

questions.text: The HOTTEST place on Earth (Dallol) is located in Ethiopia's:
questions.explanation: DALLLOL in the AFAR region (part of the Rift Valley) holds the record for the highest average annual temperature on Earth. It's a hydrothermal area with hot springs, salt deposits, and active volcanic features — evidence of ongoing CENOZOIC geological activity.
